output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause fix in org.owasp.validator.css (per the alert's regression_hint), not a downstream/sink-only patch:

1. CssValidator.java: added `lexicalValueToOutputString(LexicalUnit)` — like the existing `lexicalValueToString` (still used unchanged for policy-regex validation) but HTML-entity-encodes '"','\'','<','>','&' found in SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI token values before they go into generated CSS output. Deliberately never wraps escaped content in raw quote characters (would itself be an attribute-breakout vector); the pre-existing space-triggered raw-quote wrapping is preserved only for values that contain no dangerous characters, keeping existing behavior (e.g. issue29 test: `font-family: "Arial Unicode MS";`) byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. CssValidator.java: added `escapeSelectorForOutput(String)` — neutralizes only literal '<' in selector/condition text (the one character that can make CSS-derived <style>-tag content be mistaken for markup by an HTML parser); '>' is deliberately left alone since it is needed verbatim for the CSS child-combinator.
3. CssHandler.java: property() now calls `lexicalValueToOutputString` instead of `lexicalValueToString` when appending a value to the shared "clean" stylesheet buffer; startSelector() now escapes `selectorName` via `escapeSelectorForOutput` before appending it. Since CssHandler.property()/startSelector() are shared by both scanInlineStyle (style attribute) and scanStyleSheet (<style> tag), this closes both DOM sinks named in the alert (AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:517 and :425-431) plus the SAC_URI branch, from one shared fix point — no changes needed in AntiSamyDOMScanner.java itself.
4. Added 3 regression tests to AntiSamyTest.java, verified to fail on pre-patch code and pass post-patch: (a) default-policy embedded quote in font-family no longer reaches the raw DOM style Attr value unescaped; (b) a widened/custom font-family policy no longer lets a literal <script> tag reach the raw DOM style Attr value; (c) same check for the sibling <style>-tag Text node sink.

Validated: `mvn -B -DskipTests package` succeeds; `mvn -B test` — 103/103 tests pass (100 pre-existing + 3 new); the provided PoV (`bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`) now prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (was exit 0/VULNERABLE before the patch).
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change is intentionally scoped to CSS values/selectors that contain '\"', '\\'', '<', '>', or '&' — the overwhelming majority of legitimate CSS (colors, lengths, keywords, ordinary font names, combinators, etc.) is untouched, confirmed by the full existing test suite passing unchanged. For the rare case where a CSS string value legitimately embeds one of these 5 characters (e.g. a font-family name containing a literal quote), the "clean" output now shows an HTML entity (e.g. `"`) instead of the raw character; within a <style> tag (RAWTEXT, no entity decoding by the browser) this renders as literal entity text rather than being interpreted, which is a minor cosmetic/functional trade-off accepted in exchange for closing the XSS. No changes were made to policy validation logic (`lexicalValueToString`, `isValidProperty`, `isValidSelector`, `isValidCondition` all still operate on raw values), so which CSS is accepted/rejected by a given policy is unaffected — only how already-accepted CSS-derived text is serialized into the DOM changed.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-079 (CSS-to-DOM XSS) at its root cause: org.owasp.validator.css.CssHandler was writing CSS-derived text (property values, URLs, selectors) into the "clean" stylesheet buffer with zero HTML-neutralization, relying entirely on a downstream, optional HTML serializer to escape it. That "clean" text is written verbatim into DOM Attr/Text node values by AntiSamyDOMScanner (both the "style" attribute sink and the sibling <style>-tag text-node sink), so any consumer of the public CleanResults.getCleanXMLDocumentFragment() API received raw, unescaped HTML-significant characters ('"', ''', '<', '>', '&') that originated from attacker-controlled CSS. Added CssValidator.lexicalValueToOutputString() (HTML-entity-encodes those 5 characters for SAC_STRING_VALUE/SAC_IDENT/SAC_URI lexical values, leaving CSS structural syntax untouched) and CssValidator.escapeSelectorForOutput() (neutralizes only '<' in selector/condition text, since '>' must remain literal for child-combinator selectors). Wired both into CssHandler.property() and CssHandler.startSelector(), the two places that build the shared "clean" CSS text consumed by both the inline style-attribute path and the <style>-tag path — closing the finder's primary trace plus the SAC_URI branch and the sibling <style>-tag/selector paths called out in the alert as sharing the same root cause.
